title: An element cutting the support of a Cohen–Macaulay module by one dimension is a nonzerodivisor on it
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$). For a finite $R$-module $N$ let $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$ be the set of prime ideals $\mathfrak p\subset R$ with $N_{\mathfrak p}\neq0$, $N_{\mathfrak p}$ the localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], and let $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N)\in\{-\infty,0,1,2,\dots\}$ be the supremum of the integers $n\ge0$ for which there is a chain $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n$ of prime ideals all lying in $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$ ($-\infty$ when $\operatorname{Supp}(N)=\emptyset$, i.e. $N=0$; the same definition for any subset of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ in place of $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$). Let $M\neq0$ be a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] which is Cohen–Macaulay, i.e. $\operatorname{depth}(M)=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)$, where $\operatorname{depth}(M)=\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}(M)$ is the depth [def-weil-pbc-depth]. Let $g\in\mathfrak m$ and let $V(g)$ be the set of prime ideals of $R$ containing $g$; suppose that $\dim\bigl(\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(g)\bigr)=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)-1$. Then (a) $g$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M$ (multiplication by $g$ on $M$ is injective), and (b) $M/gM$ is Cohen–Macaulay with $\operatorname{depth}(M/gM)=\operatorname{depth}(M)-1$.

proof.text:
(Notation; $d$ is a positive integer; a maximal regular sequence.) Write $d=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)$. Since $R$ is local, every $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak m$ is a unit, so the localization map $M	o M_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] is bijective ($m/s=s^{-1}m/1$, and $tm=0$ with $t$ a unit forces $m=0$); as $M
eq0$, $\mathfrak m\in\operatorname{Supp}(M)$. A chain of primes in $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ is a chain of primes of $R$, so $0\le d\le\dim R$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and $\dim R$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension]; thus $d$ is an integer $\ge0$. Moreover $d
eq0$: if $d=0$, the hypothesis says $\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(g))=-1$, which is impossible since $\mathfrak m\in\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(g)$ (as $g\in\mathfrak m$) makes this set nonempty, of dimension $\ge0$ (Stacks: 'The case $d=0$ does not occur'). So $d\ge1$. Since $\operatorname{depth}(M)=d$ is finite, by [def-weil-pbc-depth] we have $\mathfrak mM
eq M$ and $d$ is the supremum of the lengths of the $M$-regular sequences in $\mathfrak m$; a supremum of a set of integers that equals the integer $d$ is attained, so there is an $M$-regular sequence $f_1,\dots,f_d\in\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] (Stacks: 'Choose a $M$-regular sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_d$ with $d=\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(M))$').

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00N5 (lemma-CM-one-g, line 25018), proof lines 25026-25048

proof.text: (The claim proved by induction on $d$.) For an integer $e\ge1$ let $P(e)$ be the assertion: for every nonzero finite Cohen–Macaulay $R$-module $N$ with $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N)=e$ and every $y\in\mathfrak m$ with $\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(N)\cap V(y))=e-1$, (a) $y$ is a nonzerodivisor on $N$ and (b) $N/yN$ is Cohen–Macaulay with $\operatorname{depth}(N/yN)=\operatorname{depth}(N)-1$. By step 1 the item is the statement that $P(e)$ holds for all $e\ge1$. We prove $P(1)$ (step 3) and, for $e\ge2$, $P(e-1)\Rightarrow P(e)$ (steps 4-9, written for $N=M$, $y=g$, $e=d\ge2$, with $f_1,\dots,f_d$ as in step 1; only the hypotheses of $P(d)$ are used, and step 1 applies to any such $N$, $y$). This is the induction on $d$ of the source ('the pair $(M/hM,g)$ satisfies the induction hypothesis').

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00N5 (lemma-CM-one-g, line 25018), proof lines 25026-25048

proof.text: (If $g$ is good, in particular if $d=1$.) Suppose $g$ is good with respect to $(M,f_1,\dots,f_d)$, i.e. $\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(g,f_1,\dots,f_i))=d-i-1$ for $i=0,\dots,d-1$. Then [lem-weil-pbc-cm-module-good-sequence-element-nonzerodivisor] gives (a) $g$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M$, and (b) $M/gM$ is Cohen–Macaulay with $\operatorname{depth}(M/gM)=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M/gM)=d-1=\operatorname{depth}(M)-1$; so the item holds ('we win by Lemma 00N4'). For $d=1$ the goodness condition consists of the single case $i=0$, $\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(g))=0=d-1$, which is the hypothesis; hence $P(1)$ holds ('In particular the lemma holds if $d=1$'). From now on $d\ge2$ and we assume $P(d-1)$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00N5 (lemma-CM-one-g, line 25018), proof lines 25026-25048

proof.text: (The supports involved and their dimensions.) For $0\le i\le d$ put $M_i=M/(f_1,\dots,f_i)M$ (so $M_0=M$), a finite $R$-module, and note $M_i\cong M_{i-1}/f_iM_{i-1}$ for $i\ge1$ (the submodule $(f_1,\dots,f_i)M$ is the preimage in $M$ of $f_iM_{i-1}$). By [lem-weil-pbc-support-quotient-ideal-module] (with $I=(f_1,\dots,f_i)$, resp. $I=(g)$), $\operatorname{Supp}(M_i)=\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(f_1,\dots,f_i)$ and $\operatorname{Supp}(M/gM)=\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(g)$. By the definition of a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], $f_i\in\mathfrak m$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M_{i-1}$ for $1\le i\le d$, so clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-support-dimension-quotient-element-equality] gives $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M_i)+1=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M_{i-1})$; by induction on $i$ from $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M_0)=d$, $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M_i)=d-i$ for $0\le i\le d$. Also $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M/gM)=d-1$ by the hypothesis. In particular the $d+1$ modules $N\in\{M_0,\dots,M_{d-1},M/gM\}$ all have $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N)\ge1$, as $d-i\ge1$ for $i\le d-1$ and $d-1\ge1$. These $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$ are the closed sets $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$, $\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(f_1,\dots,f_i)$ ($1\le i\le d-1$) and $\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(g)$ of the source.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00N5 (lemma-CM-one-g, line 25018), proof lines 25026-25048

proof.text:
(Choice of $h$ by prime avoidance.) For each $N$ of step 4, $\operatorname{Supp}(N)=V(\operatorname{Ann}_R(N))$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-support-annihilator], so the minimal elements of the closed set $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$ are the primes minimal over $\operatorname{Ann}_R(N)$. These correspond (by $\mathfrak q\mapsto\mathfrak q/\operatorname{Ann}_R(N)$) to the minimal prime ideals of $R/\operatorname{Ann}_R(N)$, which is Noetherian (its ideals are the images of the ideals of $R$ containing $\operatorname{Ann}_R(N)$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]); by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes] there are finitely many. Let $\mathfrak q_1,\dots,\mathfrak q_r$ be all primes minimal over $\operatorname{Ann}_R(N)$ for the $d+1$ modules $N$ of step 4 (a finite list; $r\ge1$ since $\operatorname{Supp}(M)
eq\emptyset$). No $\mathfrak q_j$ equals $\mathfrak m$: if $\mathfrak m$ were minimal over $\operatorname{Ann}_R(N)$, then every prime $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Supp}(N)=V(\operatorname{Ann}_R(N))$ satisfies $\operatorname{Ann}_R(N)\subseteq\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak m$ ($R$ local), hence $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m$, so $\operatorname{Supp}(N)=\{\mathfrak m\}$ and $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N)=0$, contradicting step 4. As $\mathfrak q_j\subsetneq\mathfrak m$, $\mathfrak m
ot\subseteq\mathfrak q_j$ for every $j$, and prime avoidance [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] (with $J=\mathfrak m$ and the primes $\mathfrak q_j$) gives $h\in\mathfrak m$ with $h
otin\mathfrak q_j$ for all $j$ (Stacks: 'None of these $\mathfrak q_j$ is equal to $\mathfrak m$ and hence we may find $h\in\mathfrak m$, $h
otin\mathfrak q_j$ by Lemma 00DS').

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00N5 (lemma-CM-one-g, line 25018), proof lines 25026-25048

proof.text: ($h$ satisfies (i) and (ii).) Let $N$ be one of the modules of step 4. Since $h\in\mathfrak m$ lies in no prime minimal over $\operatorname{Ann}_R(N)$, clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-support-dimension-quotient-element-equality] gives $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N/hN)=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N)-1$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-support-quotient-ideal-module] $\operatorname{Supp}(N/hN)=\operatorname{Supp}(N)\cap V(h)$. For $N=M_i$ ($0\le i\le d-1$) this reads, with step 4 and $V(f_1,\dots,f_i)\cap V(h)=V(h,f_1,\dots,f_i)$: (i) $\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(h,f_1,\dots,f_i))=d-i-1$ for $i=0,\dots,d-1$, i.e. $h$ is good with respect to $(M,f_1,\dots,f_d)$. For $N=M/gM$: (ii) $\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(h,g))=(d-1)-1=d-2$ (Stacks: 'It is clear that $h$ satisfies (i) and (ii)').

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00N5 (lemma-CM-one-g, line 25018), proof lines 25026-25048

proof.text: ($M/hM$ and the induction hypothesis.) By (i) and [lem-weil-pbc-cm-module-good-sequence-element-nonzerodivisor] applied to $h$: $h$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M$, and $M':=M/hM$ is Cohen–Macaulay with $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M')=d-1$. So $M'$ is a nonzero (its support has dimension $d-1\ge1$, so is nonempty) finite Cohen–Macaulay $R$-module with $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M')=d-1$, $g\in\mathfrak m$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-support-quotient-ideal-module] $\operatorname{Supp}(M')\cap V(g)=\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(h)\cap V(g)=\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(h,g)$, of dimension $d-2=(d-1)-1$ by (ii). Hence $P(d-1)$ applies to $(M',g)$: $g$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M/hM$, and $M'/gM'=M/(h,g)M$ is Cohen–Macaulay with $\operatorname{depth}(M/(h,g)M)=\operatorname{depth}(M')-1=d-2$ (and $\operatorname{Supp}(M/(h,g)M)=\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(h,g)$ is nonempty, of dimension $d-2\ge0$, so $M/(h,g)M\neq0$).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00N5 (lemma-CM-one-g, line 25018), proof lines 25026-25048

proof.text: ((a): $g$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M$, and $h$ on $M/gM$.) By step 7, $h$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M$, $g$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M/hM$, and $M/(h,g)M\neq0$: so $h,g$ is an $M$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-permutation-noetherian-local] ($R$ Noetherian local, $M$ finite), $g,h$ is an $M$-regular sequence: $g$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M$, which is (a), and $h$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M/gM$ (Stacks: 'By Lemma 00LJ we see that $g:M\to M$ and $h:M/gM\to M/gM$ are injective').

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00N5 (lemma-CM-one-g, line 25018), proof lines 25026-25048

proof.text: ((b): $M/gM$ is Cohen–Macaulay of depth $d-1$.) Put $\bar M=M/gM$; it is finite, and nonzero since $\operatorname{Supp}(\bar M)=\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(g)$ has dimension $d-1\ge0$ (step 4). Lower bound: by step 7 $\operatorname{depth}(M/(h,g)M)=d-2$ is finite, so by [def-weil-pbc-depth] there is an $M/(h,g)M$-regular sequence $y_1,\dots,y_{d-2}\in\mathfrak m$ (as in step 1). Since $\bar M/h\bar M=M/(g,h)M$ and, for each $k$, $\bar M/(h,y_1,\dots,y_k)\bar M=(M/(h,g)M)/(y_1,\dots,y_k)(M/(h,g)M)$, and $h$ is a nonzerodivisor on $\bar M$ (step 8), the sequence $h,y_1,\dots,y_{d-2}\in\mathfrak m$ is $\bar M$-regular [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], of length $d-1$. Upper bound: [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension] applied to $\bar M\neq0$ gives $\operatorname{depth}(\bar M)\le\dim\operatorname{Supp}(\bar M)=d-1$; in particular $\operatorname{depth}(\bar M)\neq\infty$, so by [def-weil-pbc-depth] it is the supremum of lengths of $\bar M$-regular sequences in $\mathfrak m$, which is $\ge d-1$ by the lower bound. Hence $\operatorname{depth}(\bar M)=d-1=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(\bar M)$: $M/gM$ is Cohen–Macaulay, of depth $\operatorname{depth}(M)-1$. This proves $P(d)$ and completes the induction (Stacks: 'Combined with the fact that $M/(g,h)M$ is Cohen–Macaulay this finishes the proof').
